content: If your doctor has prescribed low-dose aspirin (typically 81-162 milligrams per day) to prevent heart attack or stroke, you should continue taking it unless instructed otherwise by your doctor. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For less severe cases, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, it is important to undergo regular laboratory and/or medical tests, such as monitoring sodium levels, as recommended by your healthcare provider. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. Store this medication at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not freeze it, and avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If the medication is in liquid form, it may contain sugar, so caution is advised for individuals with diabetes. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may worsen high blood pressure during pregnancy (toxemia of pregnancy). It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist.
